reason: The hypothesis directly restates the well-documented contrast between Mn-rich (non-protective, porous, spalling) and Al/Si-rich (protective, slow-growing, adherent) oxide behavior in CrFeCoNiX alloys, as reported in P1, P6, P9, and P23. It proposes the same intervention (varying X = Mn, Al, Si) and predicts the same outcomes already observed in those passages, without combining findings from different papers into a new proposal, transferring the idea to a new regime with a stated reason, or linking evidence through a mechanism not already stated. The mechanism is taken almost word for word from the literature.
copied_elements: Mn high mobility and low-energy oxide formation causing pore formation and accelerated oxide growth (P1)
Mn-rich outer oxides attributed to outward cation diffusion (P1)
Al content increases resistance against high-temperature oxidation, changing oxide from Mn-oxides to Al-based oxides with protective properties (P6)
Increasing Al content results in logarithmic kinetics, suggesting a dense protective layer (P9)
Al2O3 scales grow slower than chromium oxide scales and are more stable (P23)
Al2O3 forms as the bottom most oxide layer due to highest thermodynamic energy of formation (P24)
Mn-rich alloys develop thicker, porous oxides that crack and spall (P2, P3, P25)
